summary:
The biggest story right now is the FDA's class-wide NAION warning, ordered on 9 Nov. NAION is a rare problem with blood flow to the optic nerve, sometimes called an "eye stroke", and the warning now covers tirzepatide, semaglutide and orforglipron. Every major outlet has covered it (AP, CNN, CBS, BBC, WSJ, USA Today, Reuters), so the news itself has peaked. But our audience is already asking "is my blurry vision on tirzepatide NAION?", and nobody has a calm, label-based answer yet. That makes it the top body-worry opportunity for this week. The FDA reviewed 126 RCTs and found 10 NAION cases among 78,217 people on GLP-1 medicines; observational studies in type 2 diabetes also show a signal. The angle that works is "rare, here are the warning signs, call your prescriber or get urgent eye care", not "you'll go blind".

Second: a new observational study (Lancet Regional Health Europe, more than 80,000 Italian adults with type 2 diabetes) linked stopping GLP-1 medicines to about 4 vs 2 heart events or deaths per 100 people a year. It's being covered by the Independent, Euronews and ABC Australia, and it builds directly on our best new long-form (Stopping, 8.84% CTR).

Third: orforglipron (Foundayo) Phase 3 sleep apnea results were published in JAMA at AHA on 9 Nov (AHI down 43.8% without PAP), and an FDA filing is planned by year-end. That fits the only non-Lane-A format that earns: an approved drug with search demand.

Fourth: Thanksgiving is still accelerating, now at 93 across 10 snapshots, with the peak on Nov 18–27. Funnel Shorts should start now.

The evergreen Lane A queue (injection site, dehydration on sick days, alcohol, burping and heartburn, keeping results after stopping) still has the best long-form economics. Several now have fresh hooks: the NYC needle-disposal fines, the alcohol-use-disorder review and the stopping-risk study.

ObesityWeek (Nov 14–17) could bring full REDEFINE 4 data. The topline (23.0% vs 25.5%) dates from Feb 2026, so it only counts as new if the full results come out. Retatrutide knee OA at ACR is already peaking.

Things we can't or shouldn't use:
- I couldn't verify the Nat Med tirzepatide resistance-exercise RCT (43003902) beyond its title and a UWA release, because PubMed blocked the fetch.
- Rejected: compounded tirzepatide price reports, Zepbound lawsuit pages, "research-use" tirzepatide vials, and the Lilly–Hims deal (cost and access).
- Animal-only pregnancy data (sheep study) and lithium case reports are too thin or niche to use.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and vision changes after the FDA's new NAION warning: what's confirmed, the warning signs, and when to call your prescriber
candidates.angle: Calm 'worried → answered' explainer. NAION is rare: in the FDA's meta-analysis of 126 RCTs, 10 cases among 78,217 people on GLP-1 medicines. Observational studies in type 2 diabetes show a higher risk than with DPP-4 or SGLT2 medicines. The label now lists the signs: sudden, painless vision loss in one eye, often on waking. Explain how this differs from the common, temporary blurry vision linked to blood-sugar shifts. What to do: urgent eye care and tell your prescriber. Never 'stop on your own'. Scope it to the whole class (tirzepatide named because it's included), with the prescriber line. Lane A body-worry: 'Tirzepatide Vision Warning: Should You Worry?'
candidates.predicted_peak: 0–4 days for news searches; 'blurry vision on tirzepatide' search keeps going for months
candidates.why_now: The FDA ordered class-wide label changes on 9 Nov, and more than 40 mainstream stories followed in 48 h (AP, CNN, CBS, BBC, WSJ, Reuters, USA Today). Most coverage uses alarming 'blindness' headlines and says little about absolute risk or what people already on the medicine should do. Our proven body-worry format ('Is this normal?') fits it exactly.

evidence.signal: Class-wide W&P label change; 10 NAION cases among 78,217 GLP-1 patients across 126 RCTs; covers tirzepatide and orforglipron
FDA requires the NAION warning across the GLP-1 RA class
FDA to require NAION risk warning for GLP-1 therapies
Rare eye condition prompts new FDA warning
'FDA's GLP-1 vision warning rests on mixed evidence': a source for the nuance

candidates.topic: Stopping tirzepatide or semaglutide and your heart: new Lancet Regional Health Europe study of more than 80,000 adults with type 2 diabetes (about 4 vs 2 heart events or deaths per 100 people a year after stopping)
candidates.angle: Build next to our Stopping long-form: 'Tirzepatide: Why Stopping Is a Doctor Conversation'. Observational, type 2 diabetes only, Italy, no prior heart disease, so 'linked to', not 'causes'. Pair it with SURMOUNT-4 regain and with what helps you plan with your prescriber. The message is never 'you can't stop'. It's 'make a plan together'. The don't-switch/stop/change line goes in word for word.
keywords: what happens when you stop GLP-1
candidates.why_now: The Independent (Nov 10), Euronews (Nov 11), ABC Australia (Nov 10) and Newsweek are covering it now, with a fear-led 'double death risk' framing. Our Stopping long-form has our best CTR (8.84%) and stopping is a proven demand theme. The study also echoes a March 2026 BMJ Medicine VA study (333,687 veterans, up to 22% higher risk after two years off).

evidence.signal: Study links stopping Ozempic-like drugs with poorer heart outcomes in type 2 diabetes
More than 80,000 Italian T2D patients; 4 vs 2 events per 100 people a year; observational caveat
Earlier BMJ Medicine VA study: stopping linked to lost cardiovascular benefit

Examples: 'Will I feel sick after a big plate on tirzepatide?', 'Why one drink may hit differently', 'What to say when someone asks why you're not eating'. No grocery or recipe-list angles.
candidates.why_now: It has risen in 10 straight snapshots, from 86 to 93. The holiday seasonal cycle starts now, and the playbook says to start funnel Shorts 2 days before the Nov 18 window.

evidence.signal: Seen in 10 snapshots, momentum 86 → 93

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: what's normal (redness, itching, small lumps), the label rates per dose, and when to call your prescriber
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 'Tirzepatide Injection Site Reactions: Normal?'. Give label rates per dose (6% at 5 mg, 8% at 10 and 15 mg, vs about 2% on placebo), say why rotating sites helps, and explain how a serious allergic reaction differs (post-marketing reports, needs emergency help). Fresh hook: NYC raised fines to $250 after workers were injured by discarded GLP-1 needles, so a short safe-disposal segment fits (sharps containers, your local rules).
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; the NYC hook lasts 3–7 days
candidates.why_now: It's first in the playbook's long-form queue. The Short reached 232 views (top quartile). It's been seen in 7 snapshots (82 → 88). Bloomberg's NYC needle-fine story (Nov 10) adds a fresh hook.

evidence.signal: NYC hikes fines to $250 after workers injured by GLP-1 needles
Injection-site reaction rates per dose; hypersensitivity warning

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) for sleep apnea: Phase 3 ATTAIN-OSA in JAMA, with AHI down 43.8% at 52 weeks without CPAP and an FDA filing planned by year-end
candidates.angle: 13:00 lead Short, plus a possible long-form built like the Orforglipron video (an approved drug with search demand). Use the angle 'How the GLP-1 pill compares on sleep apnea, and where tirzepatide already stands (approved for OSA with obesity)'. Name both trials, say they're separate trials and not head-to-head, give each one's population, and say the OSA indication for orforglipron isn't approved yet.
candidates.why_now: The Phase 3 results were published in JAMA and presented at AHA on Nov 9. Coverage so far is in trade press (Healio, MedPage, MedicalXpress) plus Time. Creator coverage is still thin, and orforglipron already earns search views for us (82).

evidence.signal: ATTAIN-OSA: AHI −43.8% without PAP, −27.5% with PAP; 31.5% reached remission or mild OSA; FDA submission by end of 2026
Oral GLP-1 reduces OSA severity and improves cardiometabolic risk factors
GLP-1 pill shows benefit in sleep apnea

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and dehydration on sick days: signs to watch for, and the label's acute kidney injury warning linked to vomiting and diarrhoea (cold and flu season hook)
candidates.angle: Practical sick-day guide: early signs of dehydration, fluids little and often, why nausea can stack up when you're ill, and when to call your prescriber or urgent care. Keep the label's kidney wording exact. Evergreen wording, so don't use 'this flu season'.
candidates.why_now: It's in the playbook queue, momentum is up from 72 to 80 across snapshots, and northern-hemisphere flu season is starting. L2 11-10 covered sick days, so use Shorts to funnel to it rather than making a duplicate long-form.

evidence.signal: W&P: acute kidney injury linked to dehydration from GI adverse reactions
ERs see a surge in GLP-1 side effects

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and alcohol: what the label says, why a drink may feel different, and what new research is exploring (alcohol-use-disorder review; semaglutide addiction trials starting)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 'Tirzepatide and Alcohol: What to Know', ahead of the holiday season. Cover what the label says, the low-blood-sugar caveat for people on insulin or sulfonylureas, and dehydration and nausea stacking. Research on cravings stays 'early and being studied': the Ther Adv Psychopharmacol systematic review, and semaglutide being tested for alcohol and opioid addiction. No 'safe amount'.
candidates.why_now: Momentum held at 80 across snapshots. The Pharmacist (Nov 10) reported new semaglutide addiction trials, and a systematic review on incretins for AUD was just indexed. Holiday drinking questions peak from late November through December.

evidence.signal: Systematic review of incretin therapies for alcohol use disorder
Semaglutide to be tested as a treatment for alcohol and opioid addiction

Use the playbook figures exactly: 335 vs 335 randomized; +14.0% regain from week 36 to 88; placebo still ended 9.9% below starting weight on average. Then cover strength training, protein and making a plan with your prescriber. Title idea: 'After Tirzepatide: What Helps Results Last?'

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide burping and heartburn: why slower stomach emptying causes sulfur burps and reflux after big meals, and what helps
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 'Tirzepatide Burping and Heartburn: What Helps'. Cover the mechanism (slower gastric emptying), the label's GI rates with both arms, and practical steps: smaller portions, slower eating, not lying down after meals, going easy on fatty and fizzy foods. Say when to see a doctor (symptoms that are severe or won't go away). Ties in naturally with Thanksgiving.
candidates.why_now: It's in the playbook queue and steady at 76–80 across snapshots. Big holiday meals make it more relevant, and CNN's 'Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects' (Nov 10) shows mainstream interest in side effects.

evidence.signal: Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects
GI adverse reaction rates (dyspepsia, eructation, GERD) vs placebo

candidates.topic: ObesityWeek 2026 (Nov 14–17): full REDEFINE 4 data, CagriSema vs tirzepatide 15 mg in 809 adults with obesity (open-label, 84 weeks)
candidates.angle: Watch it, then react with a tirzepatide-first head-to-head Short if the full data show something new (subgroups, body composition, tolerability). Topline was 23.0% vs 25.5% if everyone stayed on treatment, and 20.2% vs 23.6% counting everyone who started; non-inferiority not met. The topline dates from Feb 2026, so don't call it new. CagriSema's US decision is expected late 2026, which gives a possible approval hook.
candidates.why_now: The conference starts in 3 days. A randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide is the one news exception the playbook allows, if the data are made public within 48 h.

evidence.signal: REDEFINE 4: 23% vs 25.5%, primary non-inferiority not met
Trial design: 809 adults, 84 weeks, open-label

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and knee osteoarthritis pain, what's confirmed: TRIUMPH-1 and TRIUMPH-4 Phase 3 at ACR 2026 (WOMAC pain improved by 3.7–4.0 points vs 2.1 on placebo at 68 weeks)
candidates.angle: 13:00 'what's confirmed?' Short. Two Phase 3 trials in more than 1,000 adults without diabetes who had obesity or overweight and knee OA. Give the average change in pain score, say GI side effects were common and serious adverse events were more frequent than on placebo, and make it clear the drug isn't approved and online 'research' products aren't the trial drug. Retatrutide only gets one Short this week.
